# CYTOMEGALOVIRUS (CMV)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Immunocompetent patient

Infection is rare and usually associated with minimal or no symptoms. Mononucleosis can be associated with CMV, but is more commonly associated with Epstein Barr virus. Antiviral treatment is not usually necessary as most patients recover without intervention.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Immunocompromised patient

Patients in whom the risk for CMV disease is increased include solid organ and bone marrow transplant recipients, persons receiving prolonged immunosuppressive chemotherapy, and persons with advanced HIV disease indicated by a CD4 count of less than 50 cells/microliter.

## Antiviral toxicity information

The major toxicities of both ganciclovir and valganciclovir are neutropenia. Nephrotoxicity is the major toxicity associated with foscarnet, which may be reduced by concomitant saline administration (generally 0.5-1L).
